American Roots.

A social studies project focused on helping students investigate U.S. history through evidence, varied perspectives, and the practices of historical inquiry.

Visit the UCI History Project →All projects

About the project

History begins with questions and evidence.

American Roots connects social studies learning with source analysis, interpretation, and discussion.

The project is part of the lab’s growing work in history and civics. It centers classroom inquiry so learners can examine how accounts of the past are constructed, compare perspectives, and support claims with evidence.

Project materials are in development. The UCI History Project link below provides related official UCI history education resources and professional learning.
FieldU.S. history and social studies
PracticePrimary source analysis and historical reasoning
GoalEvidence-based discussion and interpretation

Project approach

Explore the past from more than one angle.

Investigate Sources

Students learn to ask who created a source, what it shows, and what context it needs.

Compare Perspectives

Multiple accounts help learners recognize how experience and viewpoint shape historical narratives.

Make Evidence-Based Claims

Reading, writing, and discussion are organized around conclusions students can support.
